text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers.
- The Singapore government will take a two-pronged approach to prepare young people to face the future and have the right attitudes to take care of Singapore when they grow up.

- There is no reason whatsoever for Singapore leaders to use Malaysia as a "bogeyman" to threaten Singaporeans into voting for the ruling People's Action Party because it would have no effect, Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong says.
- Malaysia and Singapore should cool off the debate on the re-merger issue to avoid affecting long-established bilateral ties, Malaysian Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim says.
- One out of every three new non-landed homes in Singapore's 35 largest private projects remained unsold in the second quarter, during which curbs on property speculation were introduced.
- Malaysia's central bank is expected to announce stronger measures this week to accelerate the pace of strategic alliances and mergers among smaller banks.

- In a move that will add to Singapore's standing as a regional finance centre and help ease the shortage of long-term debt financing for Asian infrastructures, the World Bank's International Finance Corp is to establish a bond insurance agency in Singapore before the end of this year.
- Hard disk drive maker Western Digital plans to double unit output at Singapore factory by mid-1998.
